description: For a package published to npm: a repository whose .agentprofile.yml says deployment: library extends this beside the base preset in its renovate.json. The base preset's bump strategy suits an application, whose ranges nobody inherits. A library's ranges are its consumers' ranges, so bumping one moves everyone who installs the library, and narrowing a peer range breaks every app still on the older major.

packageRules.description: Runtime dependencies update the lockfile only, so the library is built and tested on the newest release its range allows while the range it publishes stays where it is. A release outside the range still rewrites it, and waits for approval as a major. A change that starts needing a newer version raises the minimum by hand, in that change.

Peer ranges widen rather than move, so a new React major turns ^19.0.0 into ^19.0.0 || ^20.0.0 and apps on the older major still resolve the library. Development dependencies keep the base preset's bump: no consumer installs them.
